facts.text: Charles Emojong was found dead in his kitchen outside Busia on Thursday morning; his TV and two phones were missing.
One heavy blow from a narrow steel bar; blood only in the kitchen.
The kitchen window's glass lies outside on the ground under it; almost none fell into the sink.
The store-room door is undamaged; muddy size-10 boot prints cross the store-room floor to the kitchen.
Achom: the store room is always left on the latch at night for the generator fuel.
Every room was searched: mattresses lifted, ceiling boards pushed up, the store-room floor dug in one corner.
KSh 18,000 in Charles's jacket and Akol's gold chain on the dresser were not touched.
Achom: "On Sunday Dad asked me to take Uncle Julius's box to Father Thomas. He said, 'If anyone asks, there is no box.'"
Achom slept in the back bedroom with her young cousin, who woke her at the scream.
Neighbours: Akol screamed from the bedroom window at about 01:15 and kept the door locked until they came at 01:40.
Neighbours: Mzee Okiror and Charles have fought over a boundary for ten years.
The neighbours: Charles's nephew Moses owed him money.
The TV and both phones were dumped together in a ditch 500 m away, unopened.
Caught in the TV cable: a fuel receipt, border station, Wednesday 23:58, paid by PesaPap from Edwin Makokha's number.
In the parish safe: Julius Emojong's locked steel box, left by Achom on Sunday.
Fr. Thomas: Achom brought the box after Mass on Sunday; he has the only key to the safe.
Records ①: Tuesday 14:20, a call to Edwin from an unknown number, 4 minutes.
Records ①: Edwin's phone on the Busia rural mast 00:45–01:40, beside a phone registered to Fred Emuria, a boda rider.
Records ①: Thursday 03:10, KSh 100,000 "deposit" to Edwin from a PesaPap number registered to a man dead ten years: the lure SIM's ID.
Records ②: Fred's bike was offline on the app 00:30–01:50 while his phone sat on Edwin's mast.
Edwin's toolbox: a tyre lever, recently washed.
Edwin's toolbox: size-10 boots, red murram in the treads.
The host and the photos: Mzee Okiror was at the wedding until 02:00.
Moses was on a Nairobi night shift on Wednesday; he checked into his lodging on Monday.
Post-mortem: one blow from a narrow steel bar, no cuts.
Post-mortem: death on Thursday between 01:00 and 01:40.
Lab: the window was broken from inside the kitchen.
Lab: the store-room prints match Edwin's size-10 boots, and nobody else's in the house.
Lab: Charles's blood in the crimp of Edwin's tyre lever.
Edwin: "I was at the border yard all night with my truck."
Edwin: "A voice offered me five hundred thousand for a box. I went in through the store and broke the window from inside. There was no box. There was only him."
Edwin: "That lever hasn't been out of the toolbox in months."
Fred: "I was home sleeping. My bike didn't move."
Fred: "Edwin said a small job, take a box. I drove him and waited at the road to watch. He came out running with a TV and no box. We threw it all in the ditch."
Fred wears size-8 boots.
Akol: "There's no box. I don't know what you're talking about."
Akol: "Yes, I knew about Julius's box. Charles made me swear. I lied because I thought you were the people who wanted it."
Okiror: "We fought about a boundary for ten years. I was at a wedding."
Moses: "I owed him money. I was in Nairobi."

reconstruction.text: Eleven years ago Julius Emojong gives his brother a locked steel box: "If I'm arrested, keep it hidden. If I'm killed, give it to a newspaper." After case 90 Charles grows afraid, and on Sunday Achom takes it to Fr. Thomas.

On Tuesday an unknown number offers Edwin KSh 500,000 to "collect a metal box from a house near Busia, and make it look like thieves". Just before one on Thursday morning Fred drops him at the house and waits at the road, his bike off the app.
Edwin comes in through the store room, breaks the kitchen window from inside and begins to search. Charles wakes and comes to the kitchen; Edwin strikes him with the tyre lever from his truck.

Akol screams from the bedroom. Edwin tears through every room, finds no box, grabs the TV and phones and runs. On the road Fred panics at the weight, and they throw it all in a ditch. At 03:10 the deposit arrives.

afterVerdict.beat: The box is opened at the ODPP in front of Halima and Julius Emojong's advocate: eleven years of Julius's notebooks, every file he withdrew, and on every page "via Adjudication".

Told his brother died for the box, Julius Emojong asks for Amani. Over two days he says: "Every instruction came in an envelope through Adjudication, through Mr. Raphael Oduya's office. I never knew who was above him."

files.text: Closed with a statement: Julius Emojong says every instruction came in an envelope "through Adjudication", through Raphael Oduya's office.

afterVerdict.beat: Amani's notebook: "Adjudication. Oduya. The man from Lands who visited Dad? Or the man who carries the envelopes?"

clockPlan.note: Three stamps (the maximum): two records requests and a warrant on Edwin's truck. Detain Edwin after the search; boots compare at once, glass (8 h) and blood (12 h) inside 24 h.
